memories.content: The user's maternal aunt keeps one spare key to the user's home.
If the door is locked, the user is accustomed to contacting their maternal aunt, who has the spare key, before contacting building management.
When going to collect the spare key from their maternal aunt, the user wants to give an arrival time first so neither person has to wait.
The user feels at ease only after returning a borrowed spare key in person on the same day.
The user feels uneasy about writing down a new entrance passcode on paper.
The user found it difficult when a family member arrived without notice during a meeting and the user could not respond immediately.
On a day their younger brother received a package for them, the user felt reassured after checking the delivery photo.
The user's maternal aunt wants confirmation that the user is coming in person before handing over the spare key.
Confirm with the user before sharing the spare key's storage location or the maternal aunt's contact information.
The management office of a multi-unit residential building does not hold a unit key without verifying identity.
The user reviewed their emergency-contact list in February 2025.
When preparation instructions arrived as a long paragraph, the user missed two items.
After changing the same content into a checklist, the user marked every item they had prepared.
The user called their mother on a weekend evening, but they spoke only briefly because the mother was out.
The user called again on Saturday morning the following week and spoke for 40 minutes.
The user sent a text to an old number for an emergency contact and saw that delivery failed.
After confirming the new number with their older sister, the user updated the contact list.
For nonurgent contact, the user's older sister prefers to reply by text when available rather than take a call immediately.
Before using an emergency contact, reconfirm the number and relationship information with the user.
The user feels that a reminder the day before an appointment gives them enough time to recheck preparation items.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate practical domains: the reference centers on home access, key handling, privacy, visitors, and deliveries, while the compared frame centers on contact records, communication timing, preparation formats, and reminders. No claims overlap enough for a cross-frame semantic relation.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame describes contact-list maintenance and verification, family communication experiences and preferences, improved preparation with checklists, and the usefulness of advance appointment reminders.
reports.reference_only: The reference describes spare-key custody and retrieval, same-day return, access-data privacy, management identity checks, passcode discomfort, unannounced visits, and delivery-photo reassurance.
